errors.english: because both are subject to error
errors.why: 'khrul ba here is logical deviation (vyabhicāra): blue and utpala each occur without the other, so co-reference fails; it is not 'error'.

fix.find: because both are subject to error
fix.replace: because each deviates from the other

errors.english: because they do not err regarding each other
errors.why: Same term: 'produced' and 'impermanent' do not deviate from each other (are co-extensive), not 'do not err'.

errors.english: just as different things like shade and other factors might engage in producing a single result
errors.why: Shade is the single result that the separate things jointly produce, not one of the producing factors.

note: Readable gist of a dense Pramāṇa sub-commentary on collective and generic terms, but the key notion of deviation (vyabhicāra) in the co-reference argument is rendered as 'error'.

errors.why: The side opens with a full sentence ('Why would the effect cease, i.e. be absent? And even if absent there is no contradiction' — this is stated by 'but if incomplete') that is not translated.

fix.replace: The statement "Why would the effect cease, that is, become absent? And even if it is absent, there is no contradiction at all" is made with "but if incomplete." As for the phrase "that is,"

errors.english: functions as a cooperative condition for fire
errors.why: The prior cold touch has fire as its cooperating condition (the text has just glossed 'cooperator' as fire); the English reverses the relation.
Read sdod pa, 'without enduring' (momentariness, cf. sdod pa'i phyogs on the next side), not 'obstruction'.

note: Follows the fire/cold momentariness argument broadly, but drops the opening sentence and inverts which is the cooperating condition of which.
Faithful rendering of the Madhyamaka commentary on mind and form in conventional truth; the unmarked inline glosses are accurate, if intrusive.

errors.english: his primordial wisdom should be examined through diligent realization
errors.why: The verse (PV 2.32, tasmād anuṣṭheyagataṃ jñānam asya vicāryatām) says his knowledge concerning what is to be practised should be examined; 'diligent realization' misparses nan tan bya as the manner of examining.

fix.find: his primordial wisdom should be examined through diligent realization
fix.replace: his knowledge concerning what is to be practised should be examined

errors.english: it is because their knowledge of actions and results is similar
errors.why: This is a parity reply: the same objection applies equally to knowing karma and its results; it does not say their knowledge is similar.

note: Captures the PV argument that only knowledge of what to adopt and reject matters, but misreads the root verse on examining the teacher's knowledge and some of the reply structure.

errors.english: possessing the eyes [note: original: "spyan mnga'"] of a great being
errors.why: The epithet (khyu mchog chen po, carried over from the previous side) is 'great bull' (mahāṛṣabha), a standard Buddha epithet, not 'great being'.

note: Good rendering of the Buddha's reply on having no teacher and going to Vārāṇasī; the closing words 'text breaks off' are an editorial artefact, as the verse simply continues on the next side.
Accurate translation of the one-vehicle verses, the burning-house and conjured-city parables, and the Satyakaparivarta quotation.

errors.english: Nor repeatedly carry them with the shoulder, head, or waist.
errors.why: yang yang here means 'even if light', as the commentary glosses (khur yang du zin kyang), not 'repeatedly'.

fix.find: Nor repeatedly carry them with the shoulder, head, or waist.
fix.replace: Nor, even if light, carry them with the shoulder, head, or waist.

errors.why: mdud pa dor ba is to tie/fasten the knot of the lower robe's end, consistent with the stated purpose of keeping the private parts covered; 'released' gives the opposite.

note: Sound translation of the Vinaya rules on shaving, barbering order, and deportment, with two slips in the ladder/load verse.

errors.english: because it arose immediately after being sought
errors.why: The standard reason prayatnānantarīyaka means 'arising immediately after effort', not 'after being sought'.

fix.find: because it arose immediately after being sought
fix.replace: because it arises immediately after effort

note: Literal but generally correct treatment of rival definitions of the reason and the Vaiśeṣika 'connected with that' definition; one standard logical term is mistranslated.

errors.english: This is not stated as a contradiction in itself. Rather, it means that accepting a contradiction pertains to the object of certainty.
errors.why: gnod pa is invalidation (bādhā), distinct from 'gal ba 'contradiction': this is not called an invalidator; its acceptance as an invalidator concerns an object of certainty.

fix.find: This is not stated as a contradiction in itself. Rather, it means that accepting a contradiction pertains to the object of certainty.
fix.replace: This is not stated as being an invalidator itself; rather, it is accepted as an invalidator with regard to an object of certainty.

errors.english: For example, the treatise shows that there are no valid cognitions regarding the objects of comprehension.
errors.why: 'There are no pramāṇas with objects' is the example statement that contradicts one's treatise and own words; the treatise does not assert it.

errors.english: This is the view of the (Victorious One) original: rgyal ba can.
errors.why: rGyal ba can is a proper name (the commentator Jina), not the Buddha as 'Victorious One'.

note: Follows the discussion of contradiction with scripture and one's own words in outline, but blurs invalidation with contradiction and misassigns the closing example.

errors.english: refers to the causal mental states of the past
errors.why: byed pa po'i chos / las kyi chos are the grammatical agent and object senses of 'seeking' (seeker vs. what has been sought), not cause and result.
The Tibetan says intention never occurs apart from being generated, so mentioning 'generation' is for specifying a distinction; it does not say intention arises from generation.

note: Good overall rendering of the bodhicitta definition and the eight abhisamayas, with some loose handling of the grammatical analysis of 'seeking'.
